description: Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are excluded, so only expiry times strictly between the two bounds count.

d.request: For executions joined to orders on `recordvault = ordersmark` (unmatched dropped), keep those whose `expirespot` text is strictly greater than '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and strictly less than '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', group by `ordersmark` and `orderflow`, average `fillcount` per group ignoring NULLs, then average those group averages ignoring NULLs, unrounded.
d.sql:
SELECT AVG(g.group_avg) AS result
FROM (
  SELECT AVG(e.fillcount) AS group_avg
  FROM orderexecutions e
  INNER JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark
  WHERE e.expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496'
    AND e.expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533'
  GROUP BY e.ordersmark, o.orderflow
) g;

a.request: Match each order execution to its order (where the order's `recordvault` equals the execution's `ordersmark`, and executions without a matching order are dropped). Keep only executions whose expiry time (`expirespot`) falls between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', with both endpoints excluded (comparing the values as text). Group them by order reference (`ordersmark`) and order status (`orderflow`), and compute each group's average filled quantity (`fillcount`, ignoring missing values). Then give me a single value: the average of those per-group averages (ignoring missing ones), without rounding.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(g.avg_fill) AS result FROM (SELECT e.ordersmark, o.orderflow, AVG(e.fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark WHERE e.expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND e.expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY e.ordersmark, o.orderflow) g;

c.request: For order executions that have a matching order (where the order's `recordvault` equals the execution's `ordersmark`; drop executions with no match) and an expiry time (`expirespot`) between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' (comparing the values as text), group them by order reference (`ordersmark`) and order status (`orderflow`), and work out each group's average filled quantity (`fillcount`, ignoring missing values). What is the average of those per-group averages (ignoring missing ones), without rounding? Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are excluded, so only expiry times strictly between the two bounds count.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(g.avg_fill) AS avg_of_group_averages FROM (SELECT e.ordersmark, o.orderflow, AVG(e.fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM orderexecutions e INNER JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark WHERE e.expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND e.expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY e.ordersmark, o.orderflow) g

b.request: Average of the per-group averages of `fillcount` over `orderexecutions` rows joined to `orders` on `ordersmark = recordvault`, keeping only rows where `expirespot` is strictly greater than '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and strictly less than '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' as text, grouped by `ordersmark` and `orderflow`, with NULL `fillcount` values ignored, and the result left unrounded.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(g.avg_fill) AS avg_of_group_avgs FROM (SELECT oe.ordersmark, o.orderflow, AVG(oe.fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM orderexecutions oe JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault WHERE oe.fillcount IS NOT NULL AND oe.expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND oe.expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY oe.ordersmark, o.orderflow) g;
